title: Optimizing Quantum Fourier Transformation (QFT) Kernels for Modern NISQ and FT Architectures
problem: Existing QFT compilation methods face critical challenges: SAT solver-based approaches suffer from prohibitively long compilation times due to massive search spaces, while heuristic methods produce suboptimal results in SWAP gate insertion and circuit depth for real quantum hardware.
motivation: QFT is a fundamental component in many quantum algorithms, making its hardware-aware compilation optimization critical for improving practical quantum application performance on current and near-term quantum processors.
method: The paper proposes a domain-specific hardware mapping approach using program synthesis tools to optimize qubit mappings for QFT circuits. It combines two key insights: relaxed ordering (flexibility in gate execution sequence) and unit exploration (systematic search through mapping possibilities) to generate hardware-compliant QFT circuits that minimize SWAP gates and circuit depth.
key_novelty: First approach to guarantee linear-depth QFT circuits across multiple quantum architectures (Google Sycamore, IBM heavy-hex, and lattice surgery) as a function of qubit count.
contributions: Domain-specific hardware mapping approach for QFT using program synthesis
First to guarantee linear-depth QFT circuits for multiple major quantum processor architectures
Achieves up to 53% SWAP gate reduction and 92% circuit depth reduction versus state-of-the-art
Eliminates long compilation times inherent to SAT-solver and heuristic approaches
primary_theme: QFT circuit optimization for quantum architectures
